dct_description_sm: Regional climate monitoring and modeling for Yukon shows strong trends for increasing in snowfall, earlier onset of spring conditions, and more extreme weather events. Champagne and Aishihik First Nations (CAFN) citizens have noticed changes to river ice conditions, drying up of small lakes, and ponds, and are concerned about various effects to water, the fish, and the ability to carry out traditional pursuits on the land. The objective of the first phase will be to identify climate change risk and vulnerability in CAFN with respect to: infrastructure vulnerability, drinking water quality and availability / waste water management, and extreme weather events (e.g. flooding, forest fires, storms, etc.). The second phase will focus on the development of adaptation strategies that will be incorporated into community land-use plans, community emergency plans, community infrastructure plans and CAFN decision-making processes.
